channel.title: Pier & Point · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack)
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack) (Potrero Power Station), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself…
item.description: Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources differ'); the disputes, quoted excerpts and hedging moved to this record's open questions, with every source still named. No change to the record's status or shape. Source: Pier & Point's own text edit.

item.title: Correction · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): The Stack page now says the Design for Development…
item.description: The Stack page now says the Design for Development marks the Stack in the open space just south of Block 9's outline, not inside the block, and that the Design for Development treats the land around it as Stack Plaza. Source: https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf.

item.title: Correction · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): The Stack's page now says its 1965 date comes from the…
item.description: The Stack's page now says its 1965 date comes from the 2018 Draft EIR, while press reports date the power plant to 1962 and the Design for Development captions a 1964 photo; the sources are listed and not reconciled. The open questions also now name ICA SF's 2027 plans for the Stack and the Draft EIR's wording on its condition. Source: DEIR Vol.1 (Oct 2018) Table 4.D-1, s.2.D.4, s.4.D, M-CR-5e; Chronicle 2025-05-22; SF YIMBY 2025-10-24; D4D (2020-02-26) p.14 and Standard 6.2.1; ICA SF press release 2025-10-28 and exhibition page; Port Calendar Item 10A memo 2025-11-14; DataSF building permits i98e-djp9.

item.title: Correction · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): No source says the 300-ft Stack fell or was lowered…
item.description: No source says the 300-ft Stack fell or was lowered: the D4D, the 2018 Draft EIR and the Chronicle (May 22, 2025) describe it as standing and retained. An earlier change entry, the map caveat and the map's mapping notes said a 'fallen' stack was visible in satellite imagery; they now say that was an unconfirmed reading (a standing tower seen off-nadir can look elongated) and that the map shape may trace an imaged lean, pending a check against current imagery. The map notes were also updated to match the shape, the Unit 3 'demolished' wording was removed (Unit 3 was partly demolished in 2023-24 and may or may not be retained), the DEIR's finding that the Stack is not individually significant is stated, the Prequel Park gallery is described as proposed, and sources cite the final D4D. Source: SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Draft EIR, Volume 1, 2018-10 (https://sfmea.sfplanning.org/2017-011878ENV_DEIR_Volume_1.pdf); SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf); San Francisco Chronicle, 2025-05-22 (https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/power-station-park-sf-20339020.php).

item.title: Correction · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): The Stack’s marker moved about 120 m onto an elongated…
item.description: The Stack’s marker moved about 120 m onto an elongated feature seen in satellite imagery. An earlier version of this entry said the real structure now lies on the ground; no source reports that (the D4D, the 2018 Draft EIR and the Chronicle of May 22, 2025 describe a standing, retained 300-ft Stack), and a standing tower seen off-nadir can also look elongated, so that reading is unconfirmed. Source: Esri World Imagery (satellite basemap, Pier & Point's own reading; interpretation unconfirmed); Potrero Power Station D4D, Standard 6.2.1, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf); Potrero Power Station Draft EIR, Volume 1, 2018-10 (https://sfmea.sfplanning.org/2017-011878ENV_DEIR_Volume_1.pdf); San Francisco Chronicle, 2025-05-22 (https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/power-station-park-sf-20339020.php).

item.title: Milestone · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): Developer announces plans, with… (May 22, 2025)
item.description: Developer announces plans, with Heatherwick Studio, to open the Stack as a temporary art gallery as part of Prequel Park; the Chronicle reports the park, if approved, could open by the first quarter of 2027 (May 22, 2025). Source: San Francisco Chronicle (Laura Waxmann), 2025-05-22.

item.title: Milestone · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): Final Design for Development sets the… (Feb 26, 2020)
item.description: Final Design for Development sets the Stack's height limit at its existing height, and provides that if the Stack collapses or is damaged beyond repair, the 300-ft height limit will not apply to a replacement and the land will instead be used as open space (Feb 26, 2020). Source: SF Planning, 2020-02-26.

item.title: Milestone · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): Unit 3 Power Block and the Boiler Stack dated… (~1965)
item.description: Unit 3 Power Block and the Boiler Stack dated 1965 in the 2018 Draft EIR ('both constructed in 1965'), which extended the Third Street Industrial District's period of significance to 1965 and added both as contributing resources; the DEIR's project description gives 'ca. 1965', and press reports give 1962 for the power plant (see open questions) (~1965). Source: SF Planning Department, 2018-10; San Francisco Chronicle (Laura Waxmann), 2025-05-22; SF YIMBY, 2025-10-24.
item.source: SF Planning Department, 2018-10; San Francisco Chronicle (Laura Waxmann), 2025-05-22; SF YIMBY, 2025-10-24

item.title: Existing · The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): The Boiler Stack and the adjoining Unit 3 Power… (~1965)
item.description: The Boiler Stack and the adjoining Unit 3 Power Block (dated 1965 in the 2018 Draft EIR; press reports give 1962 for the power plant) are covered by the final Design for Development (Feb 26, 2020) as existing structures: Standard 6.2.1, 'Height of Existing Structures', sets the Stack's height limit at its existing height and provides that a collapsed or irreparably damaged Stack is not replaced by a new structure of that height (~1965). Source: SF Planning Department, 2018-10; SF Planning, 2020-02-26.
